blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Local government represents the third tier of Indian democracy aimed at promoting democratic decentralization and grassroots participation.
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 accorded constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions with a three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, and Zila Parishad.
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 established urban local bodies comprising Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils, and Municipal Corporations.
The 11th Schedule contains 29 functional subjects for Panchayats, whereas the 12th Schedule contains 18 functional subjects for Municipalities.
Both amendments mandate a fixed 5-year tenure, reservation of seats for SC/ST and women (at least one-third), and setup of State Election and State Finance Commissions.

blocks.content: Local Government is the third tier of Indian democracy. It brings governance closer to the people and ensures participation at the grassroots level.
The concept of local self-government is based on the idea that people at the local level understand their problems better and can manage their own affairs more efficiently.
The Constitution of India provides constitutional status to local government through the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992.
Local Government refers to institutions of self-governance at the village, town, and city levels.

items:
• Promote democratic decentralization
  • Ensure people’s participation
  • Improve local administration
  • Implement development schemes effectively

blocks.content: TYPES OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT IN INDIA
Local Government in India is divided into two parts:

items: Rural Local Government – Panchayati Raj Institutions

blocks.content: The Panchayati Raj System is the rural local government system in India.
It was given constitutional status by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 and came into force in 1993.
It aims to establish democracy at the grassroots level.
The Panchayati Raj system consists of three levels:
Gram Panchayat is the lowest level of the Panchayati Raj system. It is directly elected by the people of the village.
Local Government is the foundation of democratic governance in India.

blocks.content: Gram Sabha consists of all adult members of a village. Functions:

items:
• Approves development plans
  • Reviews functioning of Gram Panchayat
  • Ensures transparency and accountability

blocks.content: Panchayat Samiti works at the block level. Functions:

items:
• Coordinates Gram Panchayats
  • Implements development programs
  • Supervises rural development work

blocks.content: Zila Parishad is the highest body at the district level. Functions:

items:
• Preparation of district development plans
  • Supervision of Panchayat Samitis
  • Allocation of funds

blocks.content: Urban Local Government deals with administration of towns and cities.
It was given constitutional status by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

items:
• Municipal Corporation – Large cities
  • Municipal Council – Medium towns
  • Nagar Panchayat – Transitional areas

blocks.content: Municipal Corporation governs big cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai. Functions:
Nagar Panchayat governs areas transitioning from rural to urban.

items: The 73rd Amendment added the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects), while the 74th Amendment added the Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects).
Constitutional reservation mandates at least one-third of all seats in local bodies be reserved for women.
Elections to local self-governments are conducted by the State Election Commission, not the Election Commission of India.
Gram Sabha consists of all adult members registered in the electoral rolls of a village, serving as the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system.

blocks.content: Local Government is the foundation of democratic governance in India.
Through Panchayats and Municipalities, people directly participate in administration. Strengthening local bodies is essential for inclusive and sustainable development.
